topic: Centre of Mass of Common Bodies
title: No Metal There? Centre of Mass of Common Bodies | Class 11 Physics
description:
A cricket bat, a steel plate, a bangle: each has one point where its mass is centred. For some bodies that point is easy to find. For others it is a surprise. When Aarav tapes a bangle onto a light clear square, it balances right at the bangle's centre, where there is no metal at all. How? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Physics (Chapter 6, System of Particles and Rotational Motion) we find the centre of mass of common bodies.

We pair up the bits of a uniform rod to see why its centre of mass is at its middle, and why a uniform, symmetric ring, disc, sphere or rectangle has its centre at the geometric centre, while a triangle plate has it where the medians meet. On a live motion notebook we build a bangle bit by bit: as the arc grows, the centre of mass moves in from the metal, passes 2R/pi for a half ring, and reaches the empty centre for the full ring, with the readout and a graph tracking the distance. A slow-mo replay watches the last gap close. We write the rules step by step (pairs cancel, rod at L/2, parts at their own centres, areas for plates), compare a ring and a disc side by side, and find the centre of an L-shaped plate, which lies off the plate. Then the exam trap (a hole is negative mass), an original JEE Main pattern question on a plate with a corner cut out, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE) and PUC (Karnataka) Class 11 students, and for JEE Main and NEET preparation.
